Where it began
2006
First Scopus-retrieved acknowledgment
Dönmez O., “The numerical simulation of perturbed accretion disk around the massive black hole”, International Journal of Modern Physics D (2006-07) — a black-hole accretion-disk simulation, crediting “TUBITAK/ULAKBIM super computers / Beowulf and T3E clusters”: the centre's original supercomputers, before the TR-Grid era even began.
Source-specific milestone: a different database can begin later because the record itself or its acknowledgment metadata is absent there; this is not evidence that TRUBA use began later.
Methodology
ⓘ Methodology & data — how these numbers are made
Publications crediting TRUBA / ULAKBİM computing in their Scopus funding acknowledgments. Journal quality uses SCImago SJR quartiles; citations are a snapshot at extraction, and the current year is still being indexed. Counts are a lower bound — only written acknowledgments can be found. Large-collaboration papers (ATLAS · CMS · Belle II) follow a different attribution basis and are reported separately on the WLCG page. Update schedule: the dashboard is refreshed monthly from Scopus (the latest source date is shown at the top); citation counts and recent-year totals change retrospectively as Scopus continues indexing, so month-to-month movements in the current year are expected.
Centre names: The centre has been renamed twice — High Performance Computing Center (pre-2012), … and Grid Computing Center, and … and Network Computing Center (current) — and authors still use all three. Only the middle form contains “and Grid”, so a query resting on that phrase alone misses the other two. The bare English name cannot be a search term (it matches hundreds of unrelated centres worldwide, İTÜ's UHeM among them), so it counts only when anchored to “ULAKBİM” in the same breath. A paper using a variant the term list does not carry still reaches this corpus through the ULAKBİM review queue, so the Scopus arm loses nothing to the naming problem; a database without such a fallback does.
Conference papers: SJR ranks journals, so the 85 conference papers in this corpus are counted in the totals but excluded from the quality figures — Q1 share and citations per article are journal-article quantities. The UHeM dashboard does the same, so the two stay comparable.
This is a personal research project and is not an official TÜBİTAK or ULAKBİM website.
